 Hon'Ble Sameer Jain, J. 
1.
Heard Sri Satish Sharma, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri R.N. Srivastava, learned AGA for the State.

2. The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.05 of 2021, under Sections 304B, 498A, 323, 504, 506 IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Syana, District Bulandshahr, during pendency of the trial.
3. FIR of the present case was lodged on 2.1.2021 against applicant and his family members.

According to the FIR, marriage of the applicant was solemnized with the daughter of the informant in the year 2017 and after marriage applicant and his family members started torturing her for demand of dowry of motorcycle and additional money and on 2.1.2021, they badly beaten her and,
thereafter, burnt her and after receiving information, informant and his family members arrived her matrimonial home and admitted her in the hospital.
4.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits, however, applicant is husband of the deceased but on the basis of false allegation he has been made accused in the present matter.

5. Learned counsel for the applicant submits, initially, FIR of the present case was lodged under Sections 498A, 323, 307, 504, 506 IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act but after the death of the deceased case was converted under Section 304B IPC.
6. He further submits, actually, deceased was having doubt that applicant was having illicit relationship with another lady and only due to this reason she committed suicide by ablazing herself.

7. He further submits, however, before death of the deceased, doctor recorded dying declaration of the deceased in which she stated that applicant along with his family members burnt her but as she was having doubt about the illicit relationship of the applicant, therefore, she made false allegation against the applicant and his family members and her dying declaration cannot be relied upon.
8. He further submits, in the present matter applicant is in jail since 14.03.2024 i.e. for last more than almost two years.

9. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bill and submits applicant is husband of the deceased and there is dying declaration of the deceased on record and from its perusal, it is apparent that applicant along with his family members burnt her.
10. He further submitted that FIR of the present case was lodged in the year 2021 but applicant could only be arrested on 14.03.2024 and it appears, he after the incident absconded 11.
He next submits, therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case applicant should not be released on bail.

Trivendra vs State Of U.P. on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49876569/
2 12.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.
13. Applicant is husband of the deceased and his wife died within 7 years of her marriage under abnormal circumstances and there is also allegation of torture in connection with the demand of dowry.

14. Further, there is dying declaration of the deceased on record and from its perusal, it reflects before her death deceased categorically stated that applicant along with his family members burnt her and at this stage, there is no reason to disbelieve the dying declaration of the deceased.
15.
Further, it appears applicant absconded for more than two years and there is no explanation in this regard on record.
16. Further, however applicant is in jail for last almost two years but considering the facts of the case and his conduct, in view of this Court he is not entitled to be released on this ground.
17. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, instant bail application is liable to be dismissed.
18. Accordingly, instant bail application is rejected.

(Sameer Jain,J.) January 6, 2026 S.A.
